## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the drop-in is valid and reaches the right machines. On a LENOVO/`82XQ` DMI match, both the installer leaf and the migration write the same `[Login]` drop-in. The keys and `lock` values are valid in systemd v262, and no Omarchy-shipped logind drop-in overrides them. `systemctl reload systemd-logind` re-reads drop-ins without ending the session. The new test passes on this head (6/6) and fails on the base.

Four points are worth addressing: the migration can record itself as done without applying the fix, several suspend paths stay reachable, the docked-lid key works against Omarchy's clamshell design, and the test calls the real `systemctl` and has two assertions that cannot fail.

### Migration is marked complete when `sudo` fails

`migrations/1790227635.sh` line 16 is `sudo install -d -m 0755 "$conf_dir" || exit 0`. If that `sudo` fails (wrong password three times, cancelled prompt), the script exits 0 and `omarchy-migrate` writes its completion marker.

```text
sudo install -d  -> fails
  || exit 0      -> migration exits 0
omarchy-migrate  -> marker written, no drop-in
--pending        -> nothing pending, never retried
```

In an isolated run through the real `bin/omarchy-migrate` with a failing `sudo` stub, the marker was written with no drop-in, and `--pending` listed nothing. A failing `sudo tee` on line 17, by contrast, correctly left the migration pending. Line 29 also ignores a failed reload (`|| true`), so logind can keep suspending on lid close until its next restart, and the early `-f` check stops a later run from retrying the reload.

**Impact:** on an affected 82XQ, one failed `sudo` prompt permanently skips the fix for that user, which leaves lid-close suspend and the read-only-root failure in place. This conflicts with `agents/skills/migrations.md` ("A migration that cannot finish must exit non-zero, remain pending, and stop the queue").

**Suggested change:** drop `|| exit 0` from line 16 so `-e` stops the queue. For the reload, consider the pattern in `migrations/1784970000.sh`: check the effective logind setting and set `reboot-required` when it does not match.

### Other suspend paths remain reachable on the 82XQ

The code comments say suspend "can never succeed on this model", but the drop-in only changes logind's handling of the lid and the suspend key:

| Path | After this PR (source, systemd v262) |
|---|---|
| Lid close, undocked | `lock`, no suspend |
| Suspend key, short or long press | `lock`, no suspend |
| System menu > Suspend (`omarchy-menu.jsonc`) | runs `systemctl suspend`, still suspends |
| Direct `systemctl suspend` (the issue's own reproduction) | still suspends |
| Hibernate key, default `HandleHibernateKey=hibernate`, hibernation not set up | logind falls back to regular suspend |

Whether the 82XQ keyboard has a hibernate key was not verified.

**Impact:** an 82XQ user who picks Suspend from the System menu still hits the NVMe failure the PR is meant to prevent.

**Suggested change:** if the goal is that this model never suspends, a `/etc/systemd/sleep.conf.d/` drop-in with `[Sleep]` `AllowSuspend=no` covers every row above in systemd v262. `systemctl suspend` then fails with "Sleep verb 'suspend' is disabled by config", and logind ignores suspend from the lid and keys, while hibernate stays available. The menu entry would still be shown unless it is hidden separately. If the narrower scope is intentional, rewording the comments to name the lid and suspend key would avoid overstating the protection.

### `HandleLidSwitchDocked=lock` inverts the clamshell design

logind's default for `HandleLidSwitchDocked` is already `ignore`, so a docked lid close never suspended and this line adds no protection. `bin/omarchy-system-lid-close` states the intended policy: a docked lid close "does not suspend (HandleLidSwitchDocked defaults to ignore), so it must not lock either: that is clamshell mode".

logind's `lock` action only emits the `org.freedesktop.login1.Session.Lock` D-Bus signal. No listener for it was found in the Omarchy shell or Hyprland sources at this head, so today the docked setting has no visible effect. The visible lock and panel-off on an undocked lid close come from Omarchy's own `Lid Switch` binding (`omarchy-system-lid-close` → `omarchy-system-lock`), not from the drop-in. For the same reason, a suspend-key press now produces no visible lock.

**Impact:** any component that later honours logind's `Lock` signal would lock the external display in clamshell mode, against the policy above.

**Suggested change:** drop `HandleLidSwitchDocked=lock` from both scripts. The issue recommended that key for the hibernate workaround, where it is needed; for `lock` it is not.

### Test calls the host's `systemctl`, and two assertions cannot fail

The first migration run uses a pass-through `sudo` stub (`exec "$@"`) and no `systemctl` stub, so line 29 runs the real `systemctl reload systemd-logind` on the machine running `./test/shell`. In an isolated run, a recording stub logged exactly that call. On a desktop this is expected to raise a polkit prompt (not observed live); as root it would reload logind. `docs/testing.md` asks tests not to touch the developer's machine.

Separately, the "idempotent once the drop-in exists" and "no-op on unmatched hardware" checks use a `sudo` stub that exits 1, but line 16's `|| exit 0` turns that into success. With the `-f` guard (line 14) or the DMI guards (lines 12-13) deleted in isolated mutation runs, the test still passed 6/6; the stub's "sudo must not run" message went to stderr unchecked. The `[Login]` header, `HandleSuspendKeyLongPress` and the reload are also never asserted.

**Suggested change:** add a logging `systemctl` stub to `$tmp_dir/bin`, make both stubs append their arguments to a call log (the pattern in `docs/testing.md`), and assert the log is empty for the rerun and unmatched cases and contains the reload for the first run. Fixing line 16 as suggested above would also make the current failing-stub checks fail as intended.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the changed scripts, Omarchy's installer, migration, lid, lock, idle and menu paths at this head, and systemd v262 logind source (the version Arch currently packages). Isolated command-only runs with stubbed `sudo`, `systemctl` and helpers, synthetic DMI and logind config directories: the PR test on head and base, guard-removal mutations, the migration through the real `omarchy-migrate` runner, and the installer leaf through `run_logged`. No 82XQ hardware, live session, logind daemon or suspend/resume was tested. Whether every 82XQ SKU shares the reported drive fault was not assessed.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
